comparator.name: Ancient Studies (Oudheidwetenschappen)
comparator.institution: University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (joint degree)
comparator.academicYear: Current joint UvA–VU bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official joint curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. Year 1 combines eight named 6-EC modules with 12 EC of restricted orientation choices. Year 2 combines seven named 6-EC modules with 18 EC of specialisation choice. Year 3 contains a 6-EC memory course, 30 EC free choice, 12 EC further specialisation and a 12-EC interdisciplinary thesis. The official specialisations are Ancient History, Archaeology and Ancient Near Eastern Studies, plus Greek or Latin for Dutch-speaking students. No individual restricted-choice course is invented.

core: Interdisciplinary interpretation of ancient textual, visual and material sources
Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern histories, societies and political systems
Ancient art, literature, mythology, philosophy and religion
Cultural contact and comparison across the ancient Mediterranean and Western Asia
Ancient Near Eastern Studies, Greek and Latin specialisation choices, with acknowledged UCR language-depth limits
Humanities methods, source criticism, academic writing and independent interdisciplinary research
adjacent: Archaeology, material culture, museums and classical heritage
Reception of antiquity, canon formation and public memory
Ancient history, democracy, political thought and rhetoric
questions: How can texts, objects and sites be combined to reconstruct ancient societies?
How did cultural contact shape ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern worlds?
How are antiquity, heritage and political ideas selected and reinterpreted in the present?

alternatives.label: Ancient worlds: texts, objects & ideas
alternatives.concept: Combines archaeology, art and heritage, myth and literature, philosophy, rhetoric, history and independent research to interpret ancient cultures through both material and textual evidence. This is the closest feasible UCR response, while UCR lacks Akkadian, Greek and Latin language sequences and the UvA programme’s dedicated Near Eastern specialisation.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan deliberately balances archaeology and heritage with literature, myth, philosophy, rhetoric and history.
progression: Introductory literature, communication, philosophy and archaeology precede advanced heritage, rhetoric, literary and history research. All prerequisites and planned terms pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Archaeology, heritage & public memory
alternatives.concept: Follows the official Archaeology specialisation direction through world and Greek archaeology, art history, heritage, museums, historical sources, media archaeology and public memory. It emphasises material evidence and modern stewardship without claiming UCR provides field-school training.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan contains a sustained archaeology, art-history, heritage, museum and public-memory spine supported by historical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest plan, this route shifts more than 30 EC from philosophy, classical rhetoric and literary depth into public history, museum study, gender history, sociology, media and heritage communication. Its central evidence is material culture and public memory.
progression: Art-history, history, media and archaeology foundations precede advanced heritage, museums, cultural politics and history research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; nine 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Ancient history, democracy & political reception
alternatives.concept: Develops the official Ancient History direction around empires, warfare, political thought, democracy, law, rights and the modern reception of antiquity, anchored by archaeology, myth and historical research.
alternatives.labelReason: The plan’s centre of gravity is ancient and comparative political history, democracy, law and the present-day uses of antiquity.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces substantial literary, communication, art-history and museum coursework with comparative politics, international relations, constitutional and EU law, qualitative research and political conflict. It differs from both other routes by well over 30 EC and asks a distinctly political-historical question.
progression: Political, legal, philosophical, historical and archaeological foundations precede advanced law, politics, heritage and research. All formal prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The balanced texts–objects–ideas plan is the closest feasible UCR composition. The official Archaeology and Ancient History specialisations also support two distinct, coherent UCR routes. Ancient Near Eastern, Greek and Latin directions are acknowledged in the closest comparison rather than presented as separate routes because UCR lacks the required language and regional sequences. Production stops at three feasible plans.

notes.text: The joint UvA–VU programme is a dedicated Ancient Studies degree integrating ancient textual and material sources and offering formal specialisations in Ancient History, Archaeology, Ancient Near Eastern Studies, Greek and Latin. UCR offers a substantial cluster in archaeology, heritage, history, philosophy, myth, rhetoric, law and political thought, but it lacks ancient-language teaching, Akkadian/Near Eastern depth, field-school training and the ACASA specialisation structure.
